reasons: Lake identity is United States v. Chadwick, U.S. Supreme Court, year 1977.
Lake citation display is 433 U.S. 1, matching the page citation.

defect.evidence_quote: a person's expectations of privacy in personal luggage are substantially greater than in an automobile.
defect.problem: The core Chadwick/Acevedo container rule is supported, but the black-letter assertion is broader than the disclosed evidence. It enumerates consent, search incident to arrest, plain view, and border as container-opening exceptions without disclosed supporting authority for each item. The Chadwick pincite to page 13 also supports only the privacy comparison, not the exclusive-control warrant rule, which is disclosed at pin-15.
defect.proposed_fix: Narrow the rule to the supported Chadwick/Acevedo proposition, cite Chadwick at 15 for exclusive police control, and add disclosed authority records or pinpoints for each listed exception before keeping the enumerated exception list in black-letter text.

reasons: Chadwick treatment supports the core outside-auto rule: property reduced to exclusive police control, no exigency, needs a warrant.
Acevedo treatment supports the vehicle-container carveout: a unified container rule in the automobile context.
The disclosed files support inventory through Bertine, but do not verify every enumerated exception in the black-letter list.
residual_risks: No text/<case>.txt files were supplied, so support review is limited to lake pinpoints and judgment fields.
The unsupported exception items may be correct doctrine elsewhere, but they are not verified from this disclosed evidentiary universe.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use 'high expectation of privacy in personal luggage' instead of 'full Fourth Amendment expectation,' cite Chadwick pin-15, and either source or remove the exception list.
